capture.final_message:
Unfold `Set.integer`: it is the subalgebra of the fraction field consisting of elements whose height-one valuations satisfy
\[
v(x)\le 1
\]
at every prime \(v\notin S\).

Organize the argument as follows:

1. Rewrite membership \(x\in \operatorname{integer}(S)\) using this valuation characterization. Applying it to the given \(v\notin S\) immediately gives the first conjunct.
2. For \(S=\mathrm{univ}\), prove equality with `⊤` by extensionality on elements. The valuation condition is vacuous, since there is no \(v\notin\mathrm{univ}\); hence every \(x\in K\) belongs to `Set.integer univ`, exactly as every element belongs to the top subalgebra.

The Dedekind-domain and fraction-field assumptions are used only to supply the height-one valuations and the definition of the \(S\)-integer subalgebra.
